body:
## Objective

Expose the rented Ryzen 7 9700X to ChatGPT web, Codex and CI as a **queued execution service**, not an unrestricted remote terminal. Multiple clients may submit work; the server must enforce **one admitted execution job at a time**, including preparation, builds, tests, profiling and artifact processing. A benchmark comparison owns the host for its complete experiment.

Deliver an operational vertical slice: submit two immutable Buster revisions from ChatGPT web, retrieve a durable job ID, build and validate them serially on the 9700X, run the existing paired throughput harness against frozen inputs, and retrieve raw evidence without another submission disturbing the measurement.

This is a focused implementation child of #46, not a replacement benchmark framework or a new throughput epic. It is ordinary compiler/build infrastructure. No compiler speedup or actual-host qualification is claimed by this design.

## Existing implementation and ownership

Inspected main on 2026-09-11: **`44a90fcbff44988624878aff9db3346a8bc6550b`**. Read `AGENTS.md`, the build/testing/benchmarking guides, `tools/throughput/README.md`, `DEDICATED.md`, and the native harness/qualification code. Related-issue searches were targeted, not a complete repository audit.

- #429 is **merged**: merge commit `a10745904b948f1f5cf0b990a6e7d0b6bca12624`. `tools/throughput/qualification.h::tp_host_lock_acquire` implements a stable-inode, nonblocking Linux `flock`; inherited descriptors retain its lifetime. #422 still owns physical-host qualification and real-host A/A evidence.
- That lock controls cooperating harness invocations only. It does not stop independent builds or agent commands. `DEDICATED.md` also documents that `build.c` recompiles the harness **before** its native lock is acquired.
- Reuse `throughput.c::tp_run`, `tp_compare`, existing workload generation, paired order, separate diagnostic replays and sealed evidence. Do not add a second compiler measurement loop or alter default guard thresholds.
- #426 owns empirical noise calibration, dedicated statistical policy and validated Zen 5 counter groups. #424 owns multicore CPU-set experiments; #346/#423 own additional workload coverage.
- Repository implementation remains **C, no new library dependencies or vendored code**. Build orchestration remains in `build.c`. Linux/systemd/OpenSSH are explicit deployment prerequisites for this optional service, not dependencies of the ordinary cross-platform compiler build. Do not alter the source-free GitHub broker.

## Non-negotiable invariants

1. **One execution authority.** There is one worker per host and one admitted job. ChatGPT, Codex, CI and manual routine work use the same submission path. No separate Actions/Forgejo executor, background Codex session or direct shell tool executes repository work on the benchmark host.
2. **Whole-job exclusivity.** Reservation starts before Git fetch/checkout, configuration, compiler/harness builds and tests; ends only after finalization and process-tree cleanup. Never run a build on other cores while claiming an exclusive benchmark.
3. **Ownership is server-side.** Browser disconnection, request timeout or queue heartbeat expiry never releases a running job or authorizes duplicate execution.
4. **No silent acceptance.** Missing required host facts, isolation violations, output mismatches, incomplete cleanup, OOM and incomplete evidence cannot become a successful performance result. An inconclusive valid comparison is not a regression, equivalence or an improvement.
5. **Measure compiler throughput.** Building Buster, Buster compiling its corpus, and generated-program execution are different metrics. Preserve correctness/self-host gates separately.

## 1. Concrete deployment and code boundary

Use a separate existing machine/VPS for the control plane. This prevents a burst of chat polling, request persistence, GitHub operations or log downloads from creating work on the 9700X during measurements.

```text
ChatGPT web -- MCP ----+
Codex ------ MCP/CLI --+--> control host: durable FIFO + cached results
CI/manual -- CLI -----+                |
                                       | bounded worker protocol over SSH
                                       v
                            9700X: one local worker
                                       |
                              one contained job
                                       |
                       existing build.c / throughput harness
```

Proposed source layout; these are new paths, not claims that the service already exists:

```text
tools/bench_service/
    main.c                 CLI, queue daemon and worker entry points
    protocol.h             versioned bounded messages and error codes
    queue.c / queue.h      journal, idempotency, FIFO and recovery
    worker_linux.c         local admission, systemd job lifecycle, reconciliation
    mcp.c                  thin stdio MCP adapter; no execution policy
    tests.c                deterministic state/protocol/recovery tests
    profiles/              example versioned recipes and host configuration
    deploy/                systemd units and operator installation instructions
    README.md
```

Add a `build.c` tool command, proposed as `bench_service`, to construct/test these utilities. Keep compiler construction and validation recipes in `build.c`; the queue/worker selects a named recipe, supplies pinned inputs and budgets, and records results. Do not copy compiler build commands into shell/PowerShell/CMake orchestration.

The control service listens on a local Unix socket. CLI/MCP adapters and the SSH worker endpoint use that socket; only the daemon mutates its journal. A native stdio MCP adapter exposes typed job tools. For ChatGPT web, the documented Secure MCP Tunnel can wrap this adapter **on the control host**, subject to actual account/workspace availability. Do not implement TLS/OAuth or add a Node/Python SDK to Buster for this slice.

The 9700X worker initiates an SSH connection to a fixed control-host worker endpoint. Use an operator-installed transport configuration; no arbitrary host/command fields in jobs. Prefetching, checkout and artifact transfers happen only within the admitted job and outside measurement. Reconnecting a transport does not reconstruct or restart the job.

A same-host control-plane deployment may be useful for functional smoke tests, but is not the default qualified acceptance deployment.

## 2. Durable queue and explicit protocol

Implement a single-writer append-only journal on a **local filesystem** on the control host. Each framed record has a version, sequence, payload length and checksum. Persist an accepted mutation before acknowledging it. Replay reconstructs job state and the idempotency index; only an incomplete final record may be discarded. A malformed complete record puts the service into repair-required mode, not silent data loss.

Publish artifact manifests using temporary files, file synchronization, atomic rename and directory synchronization. Keep queue/request/log sizes bounded; reject capacity exhaustion rather than dropping jobs. Retention/compaction runs on the control host or in an explicit maintenance phase, never on the measurement path.

Idempotency is `(authenticated principal, idempotency_key) -> canonical request digest, job_id`. An identical retry returns the existing job. Reusing the key for a different request is an error. Keep tombstones for the documented retention period and test expiry behavior. Do not promise exactly-once execution through an ambiguous crash: stop and reconcile instead of blindly replaying.

Initial public tools:

| Tool | Contract |
|---|---|
| `bench_capabilities()` | Profiles, limits, machine state and implemented capabilities; no host scan per call. |
| `bench_submit(request)` | Persist a typed request; return `job_id`, resolved input identities and queue position. Does not wait for execution. |
| `bench_status(job_id)` | Cached phase, last observed timestamp, reservation and completion/validity state. |
| `bench_logs(job_id, cursor, max_bytes)` | Bounded cached chunks with stable cursors; indicate when live export is paused. |
| `bench_result(job_id)` | Manifest and immutable artifact references; never substitute a previous run. |
| `bench_cancel(job_id, request_id)` | Idempotent cancellation request; distinguish requested from confirmed stopped. |

Example **proposed** request; angle-bracket values are placeholders for full object IDs:

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "idempotency_key": "pr-EXAMPLE-head-EXACT_SHA-run-1",
  "machine_id": "9700x-01",
  "kind": "compare",
  "repository": "buster14a/buster",
  "baseline_sha": "<full baseline commit ID>",
  "candidate_sha": "<full candidate commit ID>",
  "workload_sha": "<full frozen-source commit ID>",
  "profile_id": "9700x-single-core-v1",
  "toolchain_id": "operator-installed-clang-v1",
  "oracle_id": "byte-identical"
}
```

Version 1 accepts approved full commits, not mutable branch names, uploaded scripts, arbitrary executable paths or shell strings. The service derives directories/argv from installed recipes. It resolves and records the **service recipe, harness, profile and toolchain identities separately from candidate source**. Candidate code must not replace the installed scheduler or measurement policy.

Support `validate` and `compare` initially. A/A is a compare request with the same immutable compiler on both sides. Use server-approved semantic oracles for intentional output changes; do not let a request silently disable correctness checks.

MCP lifecycle/tool schema tests must cover initialization, tool enumeration, bounded calls, invalid arguments, error responses and reconnects. Submission/cancellation are write tools, not read-only actions.

## 3. Host ownership, crash recovery and process containment

Lifecycle:

```text
queued -> reserved -> preparing -> settling -> measuring
       -> finalizing -> cleaning -> finished
```

`validate` skips settling/measuring. A failure enters cleanup from any active phase. Store execution outcome separately from phase and benchmark validity.

The local worker holds a process-lifetime singleton lock and records `{job_id, attempt, request_digest, boot_id, unit_name}` before starting a deterministic `buster-bench-job-<id>-<attempt>.service`. Use systemd's service lifecycle and a job cgroup rather than tracking only the first shell PID. Run repository code as a non-login job user without scheduler/queue credentials, cgroup-management authority or unrestricted sudo. The privileged lifecycle boundary may start/stop only installed job recipes; no remote root-command endpoint.

The installed per-job supervisor acquires the existing host lease **before preparation**. Every job kind uses it. The lock directory/inode is operator-controlled and never replaced during normal operation.

### Required inherited-lease integration

A supervisor holding `host.lock` cannot launch today's harness with a fresh `open()`/`flock()` of that same file: the second open file description can contend with its own parent.

Add a narrow optional `--lease-fd N` path to `TpConfig`/`tp_options` and `qualification.h`, used with the recorded absolute lock path and dedicated-host options. Validate the inherited descriptor, regular-file identity and expected path/inode; retain the same open file description, with a nonblocking exclusive-lock operation on that description. Do not add a `--skip-lock` escape hatch. Keep ordinary `--lock-file` behavior unchanged.

The per-job supervisor passes the descriptor through `fork`/`exec` to the immutable prebuilt harness and retains its own reference through cleanup. This extends #429's existing lifetime contract instead of creating competing locks or briefly unlocking between phases. Preserve cross-platform behavior and existing native lease tests.

### Recovery rules

- Loss of chat or SSH transport: the local job continues under its existing supervisor/deadline. The control host reports last-known/unreachable state and does not reassign the host.
- Worker restart: enter `recovering` before accepting work; reconcile the local journal, deterministic systemd units and populated job cgroups. Adopt a clearly identified job or terminate it and retain an interrupted result. Never resume a partial measurement as a complete experiment.
- Reboot: identify the changed boot ID, mark the old attempt interrupted, preserve partial evidence and re-run host qualification before accepting measurements.
- Timeout/cancel: stop the whole job unit, escalate after the configured grace period, and confirm that its cgroup and descendants are empty. Do not release admission merely because the supervisor PID exited. An unkillable remaining process leaves the host blocked.
- Unknown/mismatched units, ambiguous durable state or failed cleanup: quarantine the host for operator reconciliation.

Use a per-job maximum runtime enforced locally. Do not use expiring distributed leases to decide that a compiler must have stopped. A new performance attempt requires an explicit new attempt/request and retains the failed one.

## 4. Resource budgets and benchmark mode

Initial policy is deliberately serial even for ordinary builds: `max_active_jobs = 1`. This means one job, not one thread.

Each installed profile specifies build/test parallelism, compiler workers, allowed CPUs, process limit, memory ceiling, swap policy, disk/log bounds and deadlines. Start memory-heavy build preparation with one compile admission and increase only after measured memory use supports it. Wire the relevant existing controls explicitly: `CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL`, `BUSTER_TEST_JOBS`, `BUSTER_MATRIX_THREADS`, and supported compiler worker flags. CPU affinity alone must not substitute for these budgets.

For Linux job units apply `AllowedCPUs`, `MemoryMax`, `MemorySwapMax`, `TasksMax`, `RuntimeMaxSec` and whole-control-group cleanup as appropriate. Check effective restrictions, including ancestors. CPU-time quotas are containment, not dedicated CPU ownership: accepted timing must not run under an unnoticed quota or throttling condition. Resource-limit failures remain visible failures; no automatic retry with more memory or weaker tests.

The worker does not know this rented server's RAM, CPU numbering, firmware or OS configuration yet. Require an operator-installed host manifest instead of inventing them.

For the first acceptance profile:

- One chosen physical core, one measured logical CPU, its SMT sibling excluded from other workload placement; determine topology from the actual host rather than hardcoded IDs. Keep housekeeping off that core.
- No other admitted job anywhere on the machine, including download, compression, backup, indexing, CI and unrelated profiling work. Nonessential background services/timers and administrative access must be addressed in the operator deployment manifest, not merely in agent instructions.
- One uninstrumented Clang-built baseline and candidate; identical frozen sources/generated headers, flags, SDK and workload hashes. Build both and run required correctness gates before measurement.
- Invoke the **prebuilt** native throughput binary for the experiment. Do not invoke the rebuilding `bench_throughput` wrapper between measurements.
- Reuse the harness's existing warmups, rounds, paired ordering, deterministic-output checks and separate diagnostic replays. Do not invent another statistical guard or treat the current guard's exit zero as equivalence.

The reservation spans all preparation through sealed artifacts; the quiet phase covers the measurement session. The off-host queue can accept new requests and serve cached status without touching the worker. During this phase suspend ordinary job dispatch messages, reconnect loops, log export, artifact transfers and on-host journal flushing. Persist the measurement-start boundary first; retain bounded local observations and flush them afterwards. Existing harness output/artifact writes remain part of its documented measurement contract.

Control traffic must not grow with client polling. A cancel can be delivered as an exceptional stop request; it invalidates/aborts that experiment. During a partition it stays `cancel_requested`, not falsely `cancelled`; the local deadline still applies.

## 5. Qualification, validity and evidence

Before entry, verify effective CPU placement, core/sibling topology, relevant ancestor limits, installed profile identity, available memory/storage, service inventory, and absence of conflicting execution. Use a bounded settling protocol with a maximum wait and predeclared criteria. Failure to settle must produce `not_started`/blocked evidence, not an endless wait or a conveniently chosen start time.

Capture before/after configuration and low-overhead bounded observations on a declared cadence, on housekeeping CPUs. Record the sampler's own cost/configuration. Distinguish static configuration drift from dynamic observations: frequency and temperature may legitimately vary. Do not discard a slower candidate merely because it consumes more power, memory or time. Missing required sensors/facts prevent an acceptance claim; optional observations are explicitly unavailable, never fabricated zeroes.

Check for conflicting service activity, effective affinity/quota changes, throttling, resource-limit events and interrupted collection. Retain all samples and reasons. No post-hoc outlier deletion, optional stopping or rerun-until-green. Detected unrelated interference makes the experiment invalid. A candidate OOM/timeout is a candidate/execution failure, not a sample to delete.

A scheduler cannot prove the absence of firmware/kernel noise or prevent an administrator from overriding it. Report the managed-execution guarantee and qualification limits honestly; successful locking is not proof of zero noise. Use actual-host A/A evidence under #422/#426 to establish the useful resolution of this deployed profile, including its observer overhead.

Artifact layout:

```text
job/<id>/
    request.json
    service-manifest.json
    lifecycle.jsonl
    build/                 exact argv, tool identities, logs, caches/provenance
    host/                  profile, before/after facts, bounded observations
    throughput/            unchanged native harness evidence bundle
    result.json
```

The outer manifest hashes the service inputs, profile, exact compiler/harness binaries, frozen inputs, lifecycle/host evidence and native bundle. Do not modify the harness's sealed files after collection. Hashes establish integrity, not remote hardware attestation.

Expose separately:

- `execution_outcome`: succeeded / failed / cancelled / interrupted;
- `measurement_validity`: not_evaluated / valid / invalid, with reasons;
- `statistical_decision`: the existing policy's exact verdict, or not_evaluated. Broader improvement/equivalence decisions require the policy owned by #426.

Job success means a complete requested execution, not proof of a compiler speedup. Link correctness results to the exact relevant commits/binaries; earlier CI checks are not substitutes.

## 6. Reviewable implementation sequence

| PR | Concrete deliverable | Dependency / validation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Native queue, journal, protocol, CLI and fake worker; proposed `bench_service self-test` entry point in `build.c`. | No real-host dependency. Crash-at-each-boundary, FIFO, idempotency, bounds and corruption tests. |
| 2 | Linux single worker, installed per-job supervisor, systemd containment, budgets, cleanup/recovery, inherited harness lease. | On PR 1 protocol. Native cgroup/lease integration tests; existing throughput tests unchanged. |
| 3 | `build.c` validate/compare recipes, immutable workspaces, frozen-input provenance, quiet-phase handoff and outer evidence manifest. | On PR 2; reuse #429. Exercise the actual existing harness with controlled fixtures. No new performance thresholds. |
| 4 | Thin stdio MCP adapter, off-host SSH transport, authentication/installation guide, cached logs/results and truthful cancellation. | MCP adapter can be developed against PR 1's fake worker; live end-to-end integration needs PR 3. |
| 5 | Operator deployment and real 9700X qualification evidence, including control-traffic stress and A/A results. | On PRs 2–4; coordinate #422/#426. This is measured deployment evidence, not a documentation-only closure. |

No speculative cluster scheduling, Kubernetes/Slurm deployment, database server, general remote-shell app, browser UI, automated code editing, or new benchmark workload is needed to close this issue. Multicore acceptance stays with #424.

## Acceptance tests and definition of done

- [ ] Concurrent submissions from CLI, MCP and a CI client yield one active host job and deterministic queued state. Tests include builds, validation, profiling-like fixtures and compares—not only two benchmark requests.
- [ ] An admission trace proves that preparation starts only after reservation and that no later job starts before cleanup. Test `generate`/build-directory conflicts with distinct immutable workspaces.
- [ ] Same-key retry after a lost response does not duplicate work; same-key/different-body rejects. Lost dispatch/ack, journal partial writes, full-disk conditions, queue restart and worker restart have deterministic tests.
- [ ] Cancellation, deadline, supervisor failure, a benign detached-child fixture and worker crash leave no surviving job process before admission resumes. Simulated failed cleanup keeps the host blocked. Never infer cleanup from one PID.
- [ ] Native inherited-lease tests cover parent/harness coexistence, contention from a separate open description, wrong descriptors/inodes, child lifetime and no unlink/unlock gap. Existing Linux/macOS/Windows throughput tests and Linux sanitizers remain green.
- [ ] Resource-budget propagation is tested, including the existing matrix budget that affinity alone does not control. OOM/process/disk limits retain diagnostics and do not weaken compiler gates.
- [ ] During the quiet phase, a test burst of 100 submits and 1,000 cached status/log requests creates no per-request worker activity or new worker transport messages; queued work starts only afterwards. These are functional stress counts, not claimed noise thresholds.
- [ ] Misconfigured affinity/ancestor quota, missing required facts, manifest drift and an operator-controlled background-work fixture are rejected/flagged as specified. Retain invalid runs and interrupted partial evidence.
- [ ] A sealed result replays using the existing `throughput compare`; tampering/missing artifacts fails. Correctness failure cannot be reported as a performance pass.
- [ ] ChatGPT web demonstrably invokes the real **write-capable** submit tool, retrieves a durable job ID, and later fetches that job's result; repeat from Codex. Tool enumeration or read-only access alone does not satisfy this gate. Document actual account/workspace capability rather than assuming a plan supports it.
- [ ] Actual 9700X installation records CPU/SMT topology, RAM, kernel/microcode, power-policy facts, service configuration, resource limits and exact software identities. Real A/A evidence and observed noise limitations are attached under #422/#426. No predetermined sub-percent precision claim.
- [ ] Relevant repository-required validation runs on each PR's final head; report exact commands/SHA and unavailable gates. Service-only tests do not substitute for compiler correctness when build behavior changes.

Software PRs may merge independently, but **do not close this issue after only publishing an MCP endpoint, a cooperative lock or a design document**. Closure requires enforced execution, recoverability, evidence handling and the real web/Codex-to-host vertical slice. No actual server changes, benchmark runs or implementation PRs were performed while authoring this issue.

## References

- [Pinned agent/build contract](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/blob/44a90fcbff44988624878aff9db3346a8bc6550b/AGENTS.md)
- [Existing dedicated-host contract](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/blob/44a90fcbff44988624878aff9db3346a8bc6550b/tools/throughput/DEDICATED.md)
- [Existing lease implementation](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/blob/44a90fcbff44988624878aff9db3346a8bc6550b/tools/throughput/qualification.h)
- [Existing build budgets and ownership](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/blob/44a90fcbff44988624878aff9db3346a8bc6550b/docs/agents/build.md)
- [Linux cgroup v2: resource control and populated/kill semantics](https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.html)
- [systemd resource controls](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/systemd.resource-control.html) and [process cleanup](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/systemd.kill.html)
- [Linux fsync durability requirements](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/fsync.2.html)
- [OpenAI controlled MCP tools](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/mcp-server) and [Secure MCP Tunnel, including stdio](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/secure-mcp-tunnels)
- [ChatGPT developer-mode guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/developer-mode) and [Help Center availability guidance](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461-developer-mode-and-mcp-apps-in-chatgpt). These currently differ on some plan availability; verify the user's actual write-capable integration as an acceptance test.

comments.body: Claiming only the first native durable queue / bounded local protocol / CLI / deterministic fake-worker slice for this session on `astra/437-durable-fake-queue-20260913`, based on `15b19813ca51cf993d3526acb6f66c1f51f7c377`. Read the full issue and comments (none before this claim), AGENTS and build/testing/style/workflow guides, live open PRs/branches and existing tools. #429's inherited cooperative lease is already merged; this slice will not modify it or claim host ownership. No existing #437 implementation/claim found in those reads. Real-host execution, containment, inherited-lease integration, authentication/transport and deployment remain later slices. No local compilation/tests/benchmarks will be run. CI evidence and exact submitted revision will be recorded on the implementation PR; this does not close #437.

First software slice is implemented in **PR #552**: https://github.com/buster14a/buster/pull/552

Base: `15b19813ca51cf993d3526acb6f66c1f51f7c377`.
Submitted head: `004b37f45abac67af751428bcec5b94d92300bcb` on this session's `astra/437-durable-fake-queue-published-20260913` branch.

Implemented: native single-writer bounded journal with sequence/checksum/transition validation and fsync-before-ack; incomplete-final-record recovery and complete-corruption rejection; bounded FIFO admission and lifetime-retained idempotency; pinned named fake recipes and immutable source-identity syntax; separate phase/outcome/validity; one-active token ownership, cancellation/cleanup and mandatory fake reconciliation after ambiguous restart; bounded local pipe protocol and native CLI; actual implementation fault/recovery regressions registered through `build.c`.

**Exact-head targeted validation is green** in https://github.com/buster14a/buster/actions/runs/34728887554 :
- Linux x86-64: 2,808 assertions, zero failures, both normal and ASan/UBSan.
- macOS AArch64: 2,808 assertions, zero failures, both normal and ASan/UBSan.
- Windows x86-64: 183 portable-codec/unsupported-storage assertions, zero failures. Windows journal durability is explicitly not implemented.
- Standalone capabilities CLI passes on all three hosts.
- Existing Linux throughput harness: 30 self-test and 122,587 integration assertions, zero failures.

A newly registered closed-handle regression failed with two assertions on initial implementation `cdad7b080eb972f0cdda589846de9a8f3cabf943` and passes unchanged with the fix. Logs, exact revisions, regression patch and source archive are retained in the run artifacts; the initial missing-tcc pre-compilation failure is also retained and documented. No local compilation/tests/benchmarks or physical-host execution was used.

**Full repository checks/review remain outstanding; #552 is not being called merge-ready.** The final head has normal Buster CI, self-host, compiler-throughput and GPU acceptance runs requested; targeted software tests do not substitute for those gates.

This completes the implementation and targeted fake-worker validation of the bounded software slice, not deployment or the whole parent. Real source materialization/recipes, containment/systemd, inherited measurement-lease and boot/unit reconciliation, authenticated transport/service loop, deployment/retention migration, real result bundles and physical 9700X qualification remain subsequent work. Existing #429 lease, server configuration, credentials, thresholds and production runner ownership are untouched. **Keep #437 open; nothing was merged.**

Reopened after PR #552 auto-closed this issue.

The merged slice is intentionally only the bounded durable queue/protocol/CLI/fake-worker implementation. Its own completion comment says to keep #437 open and explicitly leaves real source materialization/recipes, Linux worker/systemd containment, inherited host-lease integration, boot/unit/process reconciliation, authenticated transport/service loop, deployment, real result bundles and physical-host acceptance outstanding.

Those remaining items are active admission prerequisites for #512. A closed badge here would incorrectly suggest that ChatGPT/Codex can submit an attributable whole-job comparison to the 9700X service. Reopening changes tracking only: no deployment, server mutation, benchmark run or performance acceptance is claimed.

Host availability update (2026-09-13 UTC): the Ryzen 7 9700X is now registered as the persistent GitHub self-hosted runner `buster-zen5-9700x`, online/idle, with labels `buster-zen5` and `ryzen-9700x` (runner v2.337.0). It runs under a dedicated non-sudo account with systemd isolation; management remains over Tailscale and no inbound Internet ports were opened. Fork workflow approval is configured to require approval for all external contributors.

No repository workflow currently selects these labels. This is intentionally **host availability, not #437 completion or #512 evidence**: persistent self-hosted runners for a public repository must not execute untrusted PR/fork code, and #437 still requires trusted submission, server-owned whole-job exclusivity from preparation through cleanup, inherited lease/containment/recovery, installed recipes, immutable evidence transport, and an attributable vertical slice. Do not add these labels to ordinary PR workflows. The next repository slice should be an explicitly trusted/manual path whose job acquires the operator-controlled whole-host lease before checkout/build and retains it through sealed-result finalization and process-tree cleanup.

Claiming only the next independently mergeable repository software slice for #437: validation of operator-installed pinned recipe/source materialization plus immutable, isolated per-job workspaces integrated into the existing `tools/bench_service` queue/protocol. Branch `sol/437-materialization-workspaces-20260914`, based on exact `main` `14da1343e96ea08007842bc9a67202e36c9ee02c` (tree `250ac2b8d77eb48012e5db052a50d35c96207f62`).

Scope: failing-before native tests and the smallest C implementation for recipe pin/path/source mismatch, workspace immutability/isolation, cleanup/recovery, and generate/build-directory collision prevention. This will not add a second scheduler, deploy or mutate the benchmark host, route ordinary PR jobs to the persistent runner, run performance measurements, weaken server-authoritative whole-job exclusivity, or modify the existing #429/#593 lease contract. Linux/systemd containment, authenticated transport, quiet-phase/evidence finalization, and real-host qualification remain separate operator/later slices. I will record exact local commands/results and submitted SHA on a focused PR; this claim does not close #437.

Starting the next bounded #437 repository-side slice from current main `2c93bea971058636b742acc44f22d1f3a5c4d309` (tree `d6600ab7d200d6d7411e035104a69060b75e52f2`) after #602 removed the shared-path conflict. Current searches found no open/recent inherited-lease implementation branch or PR.

Owned scope is only the throughput harness inherited lease contract: `tools/throughput/throughput.c`, `qualification.h`, `qualification_test.h`, and `DEDICATED.md` (plus a directly necessary registered build/test hook only if independently reviewed). It will add a POSIX-only `--lease-fd` path that validates an already-held descriptor against the absolute lock-file inode/open-file-description, sets CLOEXEC before candidate exec, rejects wrong/closed/directory/different-inode/contentious descriptors, and preserves ordinary `--lock-file` acquisition. It will not add a scheduler, service, deployment, host claim, measurement result, or performance verdict.

The separately reviewed materialization slice owns only `tools/bench_service/**`; #522/#568/#569 and the machine-debug slice are excluded. I will publish only a frozen exact object after independent review and exact current-main validation.

Draft PR #608 publishes the reviewed #437 materialization prerequisite slice for #36: https://github.com/buster14a/buster/pull/608

Remote branch `sol/437-materialization-workspaces-20260914` is five commits directly atop main `2c93bea971058636b742acc44f22d1f3a5c4d309`. Remote head is `7a283fc58132d7432c045ec3a4e37a5fa556bcda`, tree `a69f50b80bf3e0149f91f25bee51244c12c54619`. The tree is byte-identical to the exact Luna-clean/integration-replayed object; only GitHub-created commit metadata reconstructed commit SHAs.
